newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Guayana state to get $4 bln investment.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Guayana state to get $4 bln investment.

text.p: Seven industrial and infrastructure projects are to be carried out in Venezuela's southeastern Guyana region for a total investment of $4.037 billion, a top government official said Wednesday.
The projects include a $378 million hot briquetted iron plant joint venture led by South Korea's Ponhang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO), Information Minister Fernando Egana told reporters.
President Rafael Caldera will inaugurate the construction phase of the plant Friday, Egana said.
POSCO is due to take a 55 percent stake in the 1.5 million tonne capacity plant with the Venezuela's state-owned Ferrominera del Orinoco taking another 15 percent and U.S. Raytheon Co 10 percent.
Korea's Dongbu Steel Co will take another 10 percent and Mexican Hylsa and Hyundai Metal Co Ltd five percent each.

Other projects include a $256 million steel complex joint venture between state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) and Japan's Kobe Steel and a $720 million iron and steel plant led by Venezuela's Sivensa.

A $400 million seamless steel pipe factory by state-owned steel company Sidor, a $1.790 billion hydroelectric dam scheme at Caruachi by state electricity generator Edelca, a $103 million project to supply electricity to northeastern Brazil also by Edelca and a $390 million road/rail bridge over the Orinoco river complete the list of projects.
Egana said work on all projects should begin before the end of the year and that 12,760 direct jobs and 40,000 indirect jobs would be generated in the process.
